category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations

formulations.name: Joint state–parameter inverse model
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Treats the neural state parameters and unknown physical parameters as one joint optimization vector.
formulations.purpose: Formalizes inverse identification under physical constraints.
formulations.relation: It extends the canonical forward PINN without requiring a separate inverse pipeline and avoids using \(p\), which is reserved for probability densities in the Bayesian records below.

formulations.name: Spatial coefficient-field inversion
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Represents an unknown coefficient as a learnable field rather than a scalar.
formulations.relation: It couples two approximators through the governing residual and observation model.

formulations.name: Constitutive feasibility and complementarity penalty
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Penalizes equality violations, positive parts of inequality violations, and complementarity residuals while explicitly imposing nonnegative multipliers.
formulations.purpose: Encourages physically admissible constitutive behavior without presenting this penalty alone as a complete KKT system.
formulations.relation: Full KKT consistency additionally includes the stationarity condition summarized in F027; this record represents a soft feasibility/complementarity objective used inside constitutive learning.
formulations.symbols: \([a]_+=\max(0,a)\): positive part applied componentwise; \(C_{eq},C_{ineq}\): constitutive feasibility constraints; \(\boldsymbol{\nu}\): nonnegative inequality multipliers; \(\odot\): componentwise product.

formulations.name: Sparse governing-equation discovery
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Represents an unknown governing relation as a sparse combination of candidate terms.
formulations.purpose: Supports equation or constitutive discovery from data under physical structure.
formulations.relation: It extends inverse PINNs from parameter estimation to model-form identification.
formulations.symbols: \(\Theta\): library of candidate terms; \(\gamma\): sparsity weight.

formulations.name: Bayesian PINN posterior
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Writes the posterior using the joint likelihood of observational data and physics/condition residual information; factorization into separate data and residual likelihoods requires a conditional-independence modeling assumption.
formulations.purpose: Infers a distribution over model and physical parameters instead of one point estimate.
formulations.relation: It is the probabilistic counterpart of deterministic composite residual minimization while making the likelihood-factorization assumption explicit.
formulations.symbols: \(\mathcal{D}\): observational data; \(\mathcal{R}\): physics/condition residual information; \(p(\theta,\boldsymbol{\lambda})\): prior.

formulations.name: Independent Gaussian residual likelihood
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Models the scalar components of the residual observations as conditionally independent, zero-mean Gaussian quantities with a common standard deviation \(\sigma_r\).
formulations.purpose: Connects squared residual penalties to a fully normalized probabilistic likelihood and keeps the dependence on the residual-noise scale explicit.
formulations.relation: Different covariance structures, heteroscedastic scales, or correlated residual models require the corresponding multivariate likelihood instead of this isotropic independent-Gaussian form.
formulations.symbols: \(M_r\): total number of scalar residual components across the residual set; \(\sigma_r>0\): residual standard deviation.

formulations.name: Posterior predictive distribution
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Propagates posterior uncertainty in parameters to predictions.
formulations.relation: It replaces a single PINN field with a predictive distribution.

formulations.name: Variational-inference objective
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Approximates a Bayesian posterior with a tractable variational distribution.
formulations.purpose: Provides scalable probabilistic inference relative to direct posterior sampling.
formulations.relation: It is the negative evidence lower bound up to an additive constant independent of the variational parameters.

formulations.name: Physics-informed adversarial objective
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Combines adversarial distribution matching with physical residual enforcement.
formulations.purpose: Constrains a distribution of generated states rather than one deterministic field.
formulations.relation: It extends physics-informed learning to generative models; the exact sign and form of \(\mathcal L_{adv}\) depend on the chosen GAN convention.

formulations.name: Physics-constrained invertible/flow model
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Combines an invertible probabilistic transformation with physics consistency.
formulations.purpose: Models complex conditional distributions while preserving trainable physical restrictions.
formulations.relation: It is a distributional extension of deterministic PINN inference.

formulations.name: Ensemble predictive mean and covariance
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Summarizes an ensemble of scalar or vector physics-informed predictions using the sample mean and covariance.
formulations.purpose: Quantifies variability and cross-component uncertainty across independently trained models, stochastic predictions, or posterior samples.
formulations.relation: For a scalar state, \(\mathbf S_u\) reduces to the usual unbiased sample variance.
formulations.symbols: \(M>1\): number of ensemble members; \(\mathbf{S}_u\): sample covariance matrix.

formulations.name: Empirical predictive-interval coverage
formulations.category: G · Inverse, discovery, probabilistic, and uncertainty formulations
formulations.meaning: Measures the empirical fraction of observations contained in nominal \(1-\alpha\) predictive intervals.
formulations.purpose: Tests interval calibration rather than only point prediction accuracy.
formulations.relation: The intervals may be Bayesian credible/predictive intervals or another stated uncertainty interval; coverage should be interpreted against the construction and nominal level actually used.
formulations.symbols: \(\ell_{\alpha/2},u_{1-\alpha/2}\): lower/upper predictive interval bounds; \(\mathbf{1}\): indicator function.
